items.stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of heat?
options: A steel spoon
A wooden spoon
A plastic cup
A rubber band

explain.why: Wood is a poor conductor of heat.
Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.
Rubber is a poor conductor of heat.

solution: Metals such as steel are good conductors of heat.

items.stem: Why are cooking pots usually made of metal?
options: Metal is a poor conductor, so heat stays inside the pot
Metal does not gain any heat from the stove
Metal is a good insulator of heat
Metal is a good conductor, so food heats quickly

explain.why: Metal is a good conductor of heat.
Metal gains heat from the stove quickly.
A good insulator is a poor conductor. Metal conducts heat well.

solution: A metal pot conducts heat from the stove to the food.

items.stem: The handle of a pot is made of plastic. Why?
options: Plastic is a good conductor, so heat leaves the handle quickly
Plastic expands more than metal does
Plastic is a poor conductor, so the handle stays cooler
Plastic is a good conductor, so it spreads heat to the food

explain.why: Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.
This is not the reason a handle is made of plastic.
Plastic is a poor conductor of heat.

solution: A poor conductor does not carry the heat to our hand.

items.stem: What usually happens to a solid when it gains heat?
options: It contracts
It expands
It always melts
It always turns into a gas

explain.why: A solid usually contracts when it loses heat.
Many solids expand without melting.
Most solids do not change into a gas when heated.

solution: Most solids expand when they gain heat.

items.stem: A sealed balloon filled with air is left in the hot Sun. What happens to the air inside?
options: It expands
It contracts
It becomes heavier
It turns into a liquid

explain.why: Air contracts when it loses heat.
Heating does not change the mass of the air.
Warm air does not turn into a liquid.

solution: A gas expands when it gains heat.

items.stem: A metal lid is stuck tightly on a glass jar. Which of these will help loosen the lid?
options: Running cold water over the lid
Putting the whole jar into a freezer
Pouring cold milk into the jar
Running hot water over the lid

explain.why: Cold makes the lid contract and grip even more tightly.
Cold makes the lid contract and grip more tightly.
This does not make the lid any bigger.

solution: Heat makes the metal lid expand, so it becomes looser.

items.stem: There are small gaps between the sections of a railway track. Why?
options: So that the tracks can contract more on hot days
So that the trains can travel faster
So that the tracks have space to expand on hot days
So that rain can flow away

explain.why: Tracks expand, not contract, on hot days.
The gaps are not there to make trains faster.
The gaps are for expansion, not drainage.

solution: The tracks expand in the heat, and the gaps stop them from bending.

items.stem: A thermometer is placed in hot water. What happens to the liquid inside it?
options: It contracts and goes down the tube
It expands and rises up the tube
It stays at the same level
It turns into a gas and escapes

explain.why: The liquid contracts only when it loses heat.
The liquid gains heat, so it changes.
The liquid stays inside the tube.

solution: The liquid gains heat and expands, so it rises.

items.stem: A thermometer is moved from warm water into ice water. What happens to the liquid inside it?
options: It contracts and moves down
It expands and goes up the tube
It stays at the same level
It freezes at once

explain.why: The liquid expands only when it gains heat.
The liquid loses heat, so it changes.
The liquid used in a thermometer does not freeze in ice water.

solution: The liquid loses heat and contracts.

items.stem: Which of the following is a poor conductor of heat?
options: A copper coin
A steel nail
An iron rod
A wooden block

explain.why: Copper is a metal, so it is a good conductor.
Steel is a metal, so it is a good conductor.
Iron is a metal, so it is a good conductor.

solution: Wood is a poor conductor of heat.

items.stem: Why do people wear woollen clothes in cold places?
options: Wool makes heat for the body
Wool is a good conductor, so it brings heat to the body
Trapped air in wool slows down heat loss
Wool lets the cold air go into the body

explain.why: Wool does not make heat.
Wool is a poor conductor.
Cold does not flow in. Heat flows out of the body.

solution: Trapped air slows down the heat lost from the body.

items.stem: What happens when ice gains heat at room temperature?
options: It freezes
It melts into water
It becomes colder
It condenses

explain.why: Freezing happens when water loses heat.
Gaining heat makes it warmer, not colder.
Condensation is a gas changing into a liquid.

solution: Ice melts when it gains heat.

items.stem: What happens to water when it loses a lot of heat in a freezer?
options: It freezes into ice
It boils
It evaporates
It turns into a gas

explain.why: Boiling happens when water gains heat.
Evaporation happens when water gains heat.
Water turns into a gas when it gains heat.

solution: Water freezes when it loses enough heat.

items.stem: A metal ball can only just pass through a ring when both are cold. The ball is heated and then placed on the ring as shown. The ball does not pass through. Why?
options: The heated ball has contracted
The ring has become heavier
The ball has become lighter
The heated ball has expanded

explain.why: Heat makes a solid expand.
The ring has not changed in mass.
Heating does not make the ball lighter.

solution: The ball gained heat and expanded, so it is too big for the ring.

items.stem: A metal ball is just too big to pass through a ring. The ball is then cooled for a long time. What happens when it is put on the ring again?
options: It still cannot pass through the ring
It becomes too big for the ring
It passes through the ring
It melts and sticks to the ring

explain.why: Cooling makes the ball contract.
Cooling makes the ball smaller, not bigger.
Cooling does not melt a metal.

solution: The cooled ball contracts, so it is small enough to pass.

items.stem: Metal rods P, Q and R are heated at one end in the same way. The pins on the rods are stuck on with wax and fall off when the wax melts. Which rod is the best conductor of heat?
options: Q
P
R
They are all equally good

explain.why: Only one pin fell from Q, so heat travelled slowly in it.
No pin fell from R, so heat travelled the slowest in it.
The pins fell off at different times, so they are different.

solution: All the pins fell from P, so heat travelled furthest and fastest in P.

items.stem: In the same kind of test, rods A, B and C are heated at one end. Which rod is the poorest conductor of heat?
options: A
B
C
A and B

explain.why: Two pins fell from B, so heat travelled quite far in it.
All pins fell from C, so it is the best conductor.
Only A is the poorest, because no pin fell from it.

solution: No pin fell from A, so heat travelled the slowest in it.

items.stem: The table shows the time taken for the wax on the end of each rod to melt when the other end was heated. Which two rods are the best conductors of heat?
options: B and D
A and B
C and D
A and C

explain.why: B and D took the longest time, so they are poor conductors.
B took a long time, so it is a poor conductor.
D took a long time, so it is a poor conductor.

solution: A shorter time means a better conductor of heat. A and C have the shortest times.

items.stem: A cup has two plastic walls with a layer of air trapped between them. Why does this help to keep a hot drink hot?
options: Air is a good conductor, so it keeps the heat in
Air makes more heat for the drink
Air is a poor conductor, so heat escapes slowly
Air is heavy, so it keeps the cup steady

explain.why: Air is a poor conductor of heat.
Air does not make heat.
This has nothing to do with heat.

solution: Trapped air is a poor conductor, so it slows the heat loss.

items.stem: Which material is the best choice for the handle of a frying pan?
options: Copper
Wood
Iron
Aluminium

explain.why: Copper is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.
Iron is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.
Aluminium is a good conductor, so the handle would get very hot.

solution: Wood is a poor conductor, so the handle stays cooler.

items.stem: A wet cloth is hung in the Sun and becomes dry. What happens to the water in the cloth?
options: It gains heat and evaporates
It loses heat and freezes into ice
It loses heat and condenses
It gains heat and melts

explain.why: The Sun gives heat. The water does not lose heat.
Condensation happens when a gas loses heat.
Melting is a solid becoming a liquid.

solution: The water gains heat from the Sun and changes into water vapour.

items.stem: A metal spoon and a plastic spoon are placed in a bowl of hot soup. After a minute, which end of each spoon feels hotter?
options: The top end of the plastic spoon
Both feel equally hot
Neither spoon becomes hot
The top end of the metal spoon

explain.why: Plastic is a poor conductor, so its top end stays cooler.
Metal conducts heat much better than plastic.
Metal conducts heat up the spoon to our hand.

solution: Heat travels up the metal spoon quickly because metal is a good conductor.

items.stem: Which sentence about conductors of heat is correct?
options: Wood is a good conductor of heat
Air is a good conductor of heat
Metals are good conductors of heat
Rubber is a good conductor of heat

explain.why: Wood is a poor conductor.
Air is a poor conductor.
Rubber is a poor conductor.

solution: Metals are good conductors; wood, air and rubber are poor conductors.

items.stem: Overhead cables hang lower on a hot day than on a cold day. Why?
options: The cables contract on a hot day
The cables expand and become longer
The pull of gravity is stronger on a hot day
The poles become shorter on a hot day

explain.why: Cables expand when they gain heat.
Gravity does not change with the weather.
Poles also expand when hot, they do not shrink.

solution: The cables gain heat and expand, so they sag.

items.stem: An ice cube melts faster on a metal tray than on a plastic tray in the same room. Why?
options: Metal passes heat to the ice faster
Metal is a poor conductor, so it traps heat
Plastic is a good conductor of heat
Metal makes its own heat

explain.why: Metal is a good conductor of heat.
Plastic is a poor conductor.
Metal does not make heat.

solution: Metal is a better conductor, so heat reaches the ice faster.

items.stem: A flask full of coloured water is placed in a bath of hot water. The liquid rises in the thin tube as shown. Why?
options: The water in the flask expands
The water in the flask contracts
The water in the flask becomes heavier
Air from the bath enters the flask

explain.why: A liquid contracts when it loses heat.
Heating does not add mass.
The flask is closed. The liquid itself changes.

solution: The water gains heat, expands and has to rise up the tube.

options: A liquid expands when it loses heat
A liquid expands when it gains heat
A liquid does not change when it loses heat
A liquid contracts when it loses heat

explain.why: The level went down, so the liquid took up less space.
The liquid was cooled, not heated, in this test.
The level changed, so the liquid changed.

solution: The level fell because the cooled liquid contracted.

options: Hot water enters the flask and pushes up the balloon
The air in the flask gains mass
The air in the flask gains heat and expands
The air in the flask contracts

explain.why: The water stays outside the flask.
No air is added, so the mass stays the same.
Air contracts only when it loses heat.

solution: The warmed air expands and fills the balloon.

items.stem: A flask with a balloon on its neck is placed in ice water. The balloon becomes smaller as shown. Why?
options: The air in the flask gains heat and expands
The air in the flask loses heat and contracts
The ice water enters the balloon
The air in the flask turns into a liquid

explain.why: The ice water takes heat away from the air.
The water stays outside the flask.
Air does not turn into a liquid in ice water.

solution: Cooled air contracts, so the balloon shrinks.

items.stem: A metal ball can only just pass through a metal ring when both are at room temperature. Which of the following will stop the ball from passing through?
options: Heating the ball only
Heating the ring only
Cooling the ball only
Leaving both in the room for a while

explain.why: The ring expands, so its hole is bigger.
The ball contracts and is smaller.
Nothing changes, so the ball still passes.

solution: Only a bigger ball will not fit. Heating the ball makes it expand.

items.stem: The table shows the time for the last pin to fall off each rod heated in the same way. Which rod is the best conductor of heat?
options: Q
R
P, Q and R are equally good
P

explain.why: Q took longer than P.
R took the longest, so it is the poorest conductor.
The times are different.

solution: P took the shortest time, so heat travelled through it fastest.

The time at which each pin falls

This is the result that is measured.

Heat travels from the cooler end to the hot end
Heat stays at the hot end
Heat travels only through the air around the rod

explain.why: Heat always flows from hot to cold.
Metal is a good conductor, so the heat moves along.
Air is a poor conductor. Heat moves along the metal.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter part to the cooler part.

Both temperatures went down.

A: Metals are good conductors.
B: Air is a poor conductor.
C: Wood is a good conductor.
D: Plastics are poor conductors.
options: A, B and C only
A, B and D only
B, C and D only
A and C only

explain.why: C is wrong because wood is a poor conductor.
C is wrong because wood is a poor conductor.
C is wrong, and B and D are correct as well.

solution: Metals conduct heat well. Air, wood and plastics are poor conductors.

items.stem: At room temperature, a metal spoon feels colder to the touch than a wooden spoon. Why?
options: The metal conducts heat away from our hand faster
The metal spoon is at a lower temperature than the wooden spoon
The wooden spoon makes more heat than the metal spoon
The metal spoon gives heat to our hand

explain.why: Both are at room temperature.
Wood does not make heat.
Our hand is warmer, so heat moves from the hand to the spoon.

solution: Heat leaves the hand faster through metal, so the metal feels colder.

items.stem: Hot water was put in three identical cups, each wrapped in a different material, for 20 minutes. The table shows the final temperature. Which material is the best insulator of heat?
options: Newspaper
Aluminium foil
They are equally good
Wool

explain.why: The water in this cup was cooler than in the wool one.
The water in this cup cooled the most.
The final temperatures are different.

solution: The water stayed hottest in the wool, so wool is the best insulator.

items.stem: A glass bottle is filled to the brim with cold water and closed tightly. It is left in the hot Sun. What may happen?
options: The water contracts and the level drops
The water turns into ice
The water expands and may crack the bottle
Nothing happens to the water

explain.why: Heated water expands.
The Sun gives heat. Ice forms only when water loses heat.
The water gains heat and expands.

solution: Water gains heat and expands. With no room, it pushes on the bottle.

items.stem: A sealed empty plastic bottle contains only air. It is put in a freezer for an hour. What will happen to the bottle?
options: It will swell up because the air inside expands
It will be a little squashed as the air contracts
It will stay exactly the same as before
It will burst because the air turns into ice

explain.why: Air contracts when it loses heat.
The cooled air takes up less space.
Air does not turn into ice in a freezer.

solution: Cooled air contracts, so the outside air pushes the bottle in.

items.stem: A table tennis ball has a small dent. When it is put in hot water, the dent pops out. Why?
options: The air inside the ball gains heat and expands
The air inside the ball loses heat and contracts
The hot water goes into the ball and pushes out the dent
The plastic of the ball melts and fills the dent

explain.why: Hot water gives heat to the air.
The ball is sealed, so no water enters.
The plastic does not melt in hot water.

solution: The warmed air expands and pushes the dent out.

items.stem: Which row shows what happens to a solid, a liquid and a gas when each gains heat?
options: Solid contracts, liquid expands, gas expands
Solid expands, liquid expands, gas contracts
Solid expands, liquid contracts, gas expands
Solid expands, liquid expands, gas expands

explain.why: A solid also expands when heated.
A gas also expands when heated.
A liquid also expands when heated.

solution: Solids, liquids and gases all expand when they gain heat.

items.stem: A dentist chooses a filling that expands and contracts by about the same amount as a tooth when hot or cold drinks are taken. Why is this important?
options: So that the filling is heavier than the tooth
So that the filling always gets hotter than the tooth does
So that it does not become loose or crack the tooth
So that the filling never gains heat

explain.why: Mass is not the reason.
That would not help.
The filling still gains and loses heat.

solution: Matching expansion keeps the filling snug in the tooth.

items.stem: A metal bench and a wooden bench in a park have been in the Sun for hours and are both at the same temperature. The metal bench feels hotter to the touch. Why?
options: Metal makes more heat than wood
Metal passes heat to our hand faster
Wood is a better conductor than metal
The metal bench is at a higher temperature

explain.why: Neither material makes heat.
Metal is the better conductor.
They are at the same temperature.

solution: Heat moves from the metal into the hand faster.

items.stem: Three identical cups with lids hold hot water at 90 °C. They are made of different materials. The table shows the temperature of the water after 30 minutes. Which cup is the best insulator?
options: Foam cup
Glass cup
Steel cup
They are equally good

explain.why: The water in the glass cup was cooler than in the foam cup.
The water in the steel cup cooled the most.
The final temperatures are different.

solution: The foam cup kept the water hottest.

items.stem: Hot soup is poured into a pot. A metal ladle is left inside the pot. After some time, the top end of the ladle is hot. How did the heat get there?
options: It came from the cold air above the pot
It was made by the metal itself
The soup gave coldness to the ladle
It travelled up the ladle from the soup

explain.why: Heat flows from hot to cold, not from cold air.
Metal does not make heat.
Cold is not something that is given. Heat flows.

solution: Heat moves from the hotter soup along the ladle.

items.stem: Why are the handles of cooking tools often covered with rubber?
options: Rubber is a good conductor, so it spreads the heat
Rubber makes the tool heavier
Rubber is a poor conductor of heat
Rubber gives off cold

explain.why: Rubber is a poor conductor.
Weight is not related to heat.
Rubber does not give off cold.

solution: A poor conductor slows the heat flowing to the hand.

items.stem: A gap is left between the metal sections of a long bridge. What is the gap for?
options: To let the metal contract when it gets hot
To let the metal expand when it gets hot
To let the metal melt on hot days
To make the bridge lighter

explain.why: Metal expands when it gets hot.
The gap is not for melting.
The gap is for expansion.

solution: Heat makes the metal expand, so room is needed.

items.stem: A rod measured 50.0 cm long at room temperature. After it is heated, it measures 50.1 cm. What does this show?
options: The rod expands when it gains heat
The rod contracts when it gains heat
The rod gained mass when it gained heat
The rod expands when it loses heat

explain.why: The rod became longer, so it expanded.
Length was measured, not mass.
The rod gained heat in this test.

solution: The length increased when the rod was heated.

items.stem: Three rods P, Q and R of the same size are heated at one end. The graph shows the temperature at the other end. Which statement is correct?
options: Heat travels through R faster than through P
Heat travels through P faster than through R
Heat travels through Q and R at the same speed
Heat does not travel through P

items.stem: Two metal blocks are in contact as shown. Block A is at 80 °C and block B is at 20 °C. Which statement is correct?
options: Heat flows from A to B until they are at the same temperature
Heat flows from B to A until they are at the same temperature
Coldness flows from B to A
Heat flows from A to B until A is at 0 °C

explain.why: Heat flows from the hotter block.
Heat flows. There is no flow of cold.
Flow stops when both have the same temperature.

solution: Heat flows from the hotter object to the colder one until they are equal.

items.stem: A cook runs hot water over only the metal lid of a glass jar for a short time. The tight lid then comes off easily. Why?
options: The metal lid loses heat and contracts
The glass jar contracts but the lid stays the same
The hot water melts the edge of the lid
The metal lid gains heat and expands

explain.why: Hot water gives heat to the lid. It does not take heat away.
The jar is not the part that was heated.
Hot tap water cannot melt metal.

solution: The lid expands, so it is no longer gripping the jar tightly.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a result of heat gain?
options: A metal rod becoming longer
Butter melting in a hot pan
Water freezing in a freezer tray
Wet clothes drying in the Sun

explain.why: This is expansion, a result of gaining heat.
Melting happens when a solid gains heat.
Evaporation happens when water gains heat.

solution: Freezing happens when water loses heat.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about heat and conductors are correct?
A: Heat flows from a hot object to a cold object.
B: Air trapped in a jacket slows down heat loss.
C: Plastic conducts heat better than steel.
D: A wooden spoon in hot soup stays cool at the top end for longer than a steel spoon.
options: A, B and C only
A, B and D only
B, C and D only
A, C and D only

explain.why: C is wrong because steel is the better conductor.
C is wrong, and A is correct.
C is wrong, and B is correct.

solution: Plastic is a poorer conductor than steel, so C is wrong.

items.stem: A student heats a metal rod and measures its length. The table shows the results. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The hotter the rod, the longer it becomes
The hotter the rod, the shorter it becomes
The length of the rod does not depend on temperature
The rod becomes longer only above 100 °C

explain.why: The length increased as the temperature rose.
The length changed as the temperature changed.
The rod was already longer at 40 °C than at 20 °C.

solution: The length rises as the temperature rises.

items.stem: Why are the fins of some heaters made of metal while the knobs are made of plastic?
options: Metal keeps heat in the heater, while plastic gives out heat
Both materials conduct heat equally well
Plastic makes heat for the knob
Metal gives out heat while plastic keeps the knob cool

explain.why: Metal conducts heat out, and plastic does not.
Metals are good conductors and plastics are poor conductors.
Plastic does not make heat.

solution: Good conductor for heating the room, poor conductor so that the knob is safe to hold.

items.stem: Wet sand is heated until it is dry. Which change is a result of the sand gaining heat?
options: The sand changes into water
The water vapour changes into sand
The water changes into vapour
The water in the sand freezes

explain.why: Sand does not change into water.
This is not possible.
Freezing happens when water loses heat.

solution: The water gains heat and evaporates, leaving dry sand.

items.stem: Four cups each hold 100 g of hot water at 90 °C. Each cup is made of a different material. The table shows the temperature of the water after 15 minutes. Which two cups are most likely made of the poorest conductors of heat?
options: P and Q
R and S
Q and R
P and S

explain.why: P and Q lost the most heat, so they are good conductors.
Q lost a lot of heat.
P lost a lot of heat.

solution: Cups R and S kept the water hottest.

items.stem: Concrete slabs on a long road have narrow gaps filled with soft tar. What would happen on a very hot day if there were no gaps?
options: The slabs would expand and crack
The slabs would contract and pull apart from one another
The slabs would melt and flow away from the road
Nothing would change

explain.why: Slabs expand on a hot day.
The concrete does not melt in the heat.
Expansion would have no room.

solution: Without gaps, the expanding slabs press against each other.

items.stem: A student holds an iron rod with one end in a flame. Soon the end near his hand becomes hot. He then holds a wooden stick the same way and the end near his hand stays cool. What can he conclude?
options: Wood conducts heat better than iron
Iron makes more heat than wood
Wood is a good insulator because it gives out cold
Iron conducts heat better than wood

explain.why: Heat reached his hand faster through the iron.
Neither makes heat. The flame supplies it.
Wood does not give out cold. It conducts poorly.

solution: Heat reached the far end of the iron but not the wood.

items.stem: A ball just passes through a ring at 20 °C. The ball is heated to 80 °C and placed on the ring. It does not pass. After a few minutes it passes through again. What most likely happened?
options: The ball gained more heat and expanded further
The ring contracted so that its hole became bigger
The ball cooled down and contracted
The ball became lighter

explain.why: A bigger ball would not pass.
A contracting ring has a smaller hole.
Mass does not change with temperature.

solution: As the ball cooled it contracted until it fitted the ring.

items.stem: Which of the following would be best for making a container to keep ice cream cold for a long time?
options: A thin steel box
A box with thick foam walls
A thin glass box
A box made of aluminium foil

explain.why: Steel is a good conductor, so heat would flow in quickly.
Glass lets heat in quite easily when thin.
Aluminium is a good conductor.

solution: Plastic foam traps air, a poor conductor, so heat gets in slowly.

items.stem: A rubber hot-water bottle and a metal can hold water at the same temperature. Why does the metal can feel hotter to the touch?
options: Metal conducts heat to the hand faster than rubber does
Rubber conducts heat better than metal does
The water in the can is at a higher temperature
Rubber gives out cold to the hand

explain.why: Metal is the better conductor.
Both hold water at the same temperature.
Rubber does not give out cold.

solution: Heat reaches the hand faster through metal.
